q: What was the finance P&L net profit for September 2026 as booked by event date, and how does it differ from the order-date net profit?
answer:
The finance P&L (event-date) net profit for September 2026 was a loss of ₹1,527,829 — ₹1,355,602 worse than the order-date net profit, which shows a loss of ₹172,227. This means the books (event-date P&L) record a substantially larger loss than the order-date view.

- What moved it: P&L net profit (event date) = ₹-1,527,829 vs net profit (order date) = ₹-172,227; difference = ₹-1,355,602 (pnl is more negative). This matters because the event-date P&L records returns, cancellations and cost postings when they hit the books, so the finance view shows the true booked loss for September.
- Why it can differ: order-date net profit attributes revenue and ad cost to the order date (so some returns/adjustments appear later), while the P&L (event date) includes returns, cancellations and cost recognitions when they post to finance — inflating the loss in the finance month. The catalogue definitions confirm P&L net profit is event-date net profit (built from P&L contribution margin minus P&L ad spend) while net profit is order-date net profit (contribution margin minus ad spend (P&L basis)).

Worth checking: run a P&L break-down for September (P&L net profit broken into P&L net sales, P&L net cogs, P&L ad spend and return/cancel lines) to see which line(s) cause the ₹1.36M gap.
